summary: Big Butte, Asotin County WA: 1950 L-4 cab on an 82-ft timber tower; cab lowered and tower taken down after 2013. WTA reports the tower deconstructed; hike to the top.

facts.design: L-4 cab on an 82-foot treated timber tower (1950); the tower has since been taken down
facts.status_note: The cab was lowered to the ground in 2013 and the tower was taken apart. Per WTA, the tower cap and leg hardware lie on the butte.

access.note: On Umatilla National Forest land; the hike to the butte is open. No tower or cab remains to climb or enter.

visit.trail_note: Walk up Forest Road 170 from its junction with Forest Road 4304: about 0.5 mile to a gate, then 0.1 mile to the top (WTA).

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Umatilla National Forest (Pomeroy Ranger District)

events.note: 80-foot native timber tower with 7x7 cab erected, per a Umatilla National Forest inventory (Forest Lookouts) and TrailChick; the Register and firelookout.com date the first tower to 1938
First established with an L-6 cab on a 73-foot pole tower (Register); firelookout.com gives the same 1938 date for the pole tower and cabin
82-foot treated timber tower with L-4 cab and catwalk replaced the pole tower
Tree fell across a guy wire during the winter of 2010-2011, damaging one of the tower legs
Cab lowered to the ground and the tower disassembled after the leg damage (TrailChick)
Three days of stabilizing and restoring the cab by FFLA members, volunteers and Forest Service staff
FFLA eastern Washington report: final touches on the cab completed
Visit on 7/02/18 found the cab still sitting on the ground

corrections.why: WTA says the lookout tower has been deconstructed; a 2018 visit (TrailChick) found the cab still on the ground. The record's 'temporarily removed' note attributed to FFLA was not checked: the FFLA lookout list was not read.
The Register and firelookout.com give 82 feet for the 1950 timber tower. The record's 22.3 m is 73 feet, the 1938 pole tower that the Register says was replaced.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register and firelookout.com date the first lookout to 1938 (73-foot pole tower with L-6 cab). Forest Lookouts (quoting a Umatilla National Forest inventory) and TrailChick date an 80-foot timber tower with 7x7 cab to 1929. The record keeps 1938 and the story reports both; a human should settle which structure the 1929 entry refers to.
The Register gives 4,982 ft (1,519 m); firelookout.com gives 5009 ft; TrailChick gives 5,010 ft. The record's 1518.5 m matches the Register.

notes_for_editor: Current status is the main uncertainty. The most recent visitor source read is the WTA page, which says the tower has been deconstructed (its image file name is dated 2024); the TrailChick visit is from 7/02/18. No 2025-2026 status source was found, and the search summary also reported no rebuild. The record's status note says FFLA marks it as temporarily removed; the FFLA lookout list was not read, so that claim is unverified here. The first-tower date conflict (1929 vs 1938) is real: the Register and firelookout.com (1938, 73-foot pole) vs Forest Lookouts and TrailChick (1929, 80-foot timber). The record's 1938 is kept. A Washington state preservation office article, 'Umatilla National Forest & FFLA Give 80 ft. Tall Gift', was found by search but returned 403, so it is not cited; its search summary gives 1956 for the 82-foot tower and attributes the damage to a 2013 snowstorm, which conflicts with the 2010-2011 tree strike in other sources. A human should check that article directly. Record claims of FFLA grants of $500 in 2013 and 2014 were not found in the pages read and are not in the story. Staffing: none reported after 2014; the Register describes 'standby status' without a date, so no staffing fact is recorded. Pages read: 7 including one 403. One web search used. No photos added; NHLR and TrailChick carry photos but licence information was not in what was read.
